justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift from what I assessed as the prevailing price level at the time of the forecast, which I placed near $237–238. For the one-day horizon, I expected very little movement and anchored close to the last observed price, with the slight uptick reflecting a mild positive bias based on recent momentum. At one week, I extended that drift marginally, acknowledging that short-term trends in this asset class tend to show some mean-reversion but also continuation depending on macro conditions. At one month, I pushed the estimate a bit higher to around $242, essentially projecting that gradual drift continues without a major disruption, which is a reasonable base case when no clear catalyst for a sharp reversal is visible.

The confidence interval widths were calibrated to reflect typical realized volatility at each time horizon, scaling roughly with the square root of time as one would expect under standard diffusion assumptions. At one day, daily price swings of roughly 2–4% seemed plausible, so the 90% interval spans about $19. At one week, that widens to roughly $38, and at one month to roughly $74, capturing the compounding uncertainty over longer windows. I also factored in that at monthly horizons, macro surprises, earnings events, or broader risk-off episodes can introduce fat-tail behavior that a simple volatility scaling would underestimate, which is why the interval feels somewhat conservative rather than mechanically tight.

There are several specific risks that could push outcomes well outside these stated intervals. On the downside, a sudden deterioration in risk appetite — triggered by, say, an unexpected Federal Reserve policy shift, a geopolitical escalation, or a credit event in a systemically important institution — could push prices sharply below $205. Liquidity-driven selloffs, particularly in assets that have seen strong inflows, can move faster and further than historical volatility suggests. On the upside, a positive surprise such as a strong macro data release, a dovish policy pivot, or sector-specific bullish news could drive prices above $279 within the month. These tail events are precisely why the stated intervals, while covering 90% of my subjective probability, still leave meaningful probability mass in the tails.
